source_snapshot.title: KHDA launches Dubai’s student protection framework for private schools: Three risk levels and a protection team in every school
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: The Knowledge and Human Development Authority (KHDA) in Dubai has launched a unified framework for student safety and protection in private education institutions, which defines the responsibilities of institutions and mechanisms for prevention, reporting and response. It also classifies cases that threaten student safety into three levels according to their degree of severity, while specifying procedures for dealing with each level. The framework includes schools, early childhood centres, higher education institutions, and vocational training and education institutes licensed by the KHDA, and covers in-person and virtual learning environments. The KHDA announced the framework during a press conference held yesterday, in the presence of the Executive Director of the Policy, Research and Programs Sector at the authority, Dr. Saeed Mubarak bin Kharbash, and the Director of the Early Childhood and Development Policies and Programs Department, Fatima Mohammed Al Janahi. Bin Kharbash stated that the well-being, quality of life, and development of learners are fundamental pillars for building the future of society. He emphasised that the framework places children and families at the heart of the social development process and clarifies the roles, responsibilities, and accountability mechanisms for educational institutions. Executive Director of the Policy, Research and Programs Sector at the KHDA, Dr. Saeed Mubarak bin Kharbash. Picture credit: Supplied He added that the framework is based on the principles established by the Child Rights Law (Wadeema) and complements existing legislation and policies in the UAE and Dubai. It also supports the objectives of Dubai Social Agenda 33 and the Dubai Education Strategy 2033. He pointed out that protecting students requires effective leadership, qualified staff, and proactive parents, in addition to establishing an institutional culture that listens to students and provides them with support. Fatima Mohammed Al Janahi said that the framework defines the roles within educational institutions and obliges each school to form a student protection team, which includes the school principal as a supervisor, and at least two student protection officers who assume clear responsibilities in this area. She explained that student protection officers are responsible for monitoring cases, receiving and evaluating reports, and coordinating with specialists and senior management to determine the appropriate action, while the school principal is responsible for supervising the protection system and ensuring the effectiveness of its systems, without directly managing the cases. She added that the responsibilities include educational and academic staff and boards of trustees, in order to ensure the integration of roles and a swift response to concerns related to student safety. She indicated that the authority will work on preparing specialised training programs for those tasked with protecting students, in addition to qualifying the rest of the staff and members of the boards of trustees to deal with cases, and follow reporting and coordination procedures. Fatima Mohammed Al Janahi, Director of the Early Childhood and Development Policies and Programs Department at the KHDA. Picture credit: Supplied Dr. Samia Al Dhaoui, an educational expert at the authority, said that the framework classifies cases that threaten the safety of students into three levels, and specifies for each the mechanisms of intervention and the parties concerned with dealing with them. She explained that high-risk cases require immediate intervention and referral to the competent authorities, including Dubai Police and ambulance services, depending on the nature of the case. As for moderately serious cases, they require intervention and follow-up according to the assessment of the protection team, with the possibility of referring them to the Community Development Authority, or coordinating with the police and ambulance when needed, and informing the KHDA to ensure coordination with parents and relevant authorities. She added that low-risk cases include initial indicators and observations monitored by the teaching staff, which do not pose a significant risk when detected, but require treatment to prevent their escalation. The institution handles them internally, while informing the authority within 72 hours. Al Dhaoui stressed that the classification gives priority to intervention for the most serious cases and helps protection teams to choose the appropriate action, noting the importance of continuous training and studying practical scenarios to raise the efficiency of these teams. Dr. Samia Al Dhaoui, an educational expert at the authority, said that the framework classifies cases that threaten the safety of students into three levels. claims.claim: KHDA представила единый каркас безопасности для частных учебных заведений, включая школы, детские центры и вузы.
В системе выделены три уровня риска угроз безопасности учащихся с разными процедурами реагирования.
В каждой школе создадут команду защиты, в которую войдут директор и минимум два ответственных сотрудника.
Они будут следить за случаями, координировать действия и взаимодействовать с властями.
Каркас основан на законе о правах ребёнка и поддерживает стратегию образования Дубая до 2033 года.

title: KHDA launches Dubai’s student protection framework for private schools: Three risk levels and a protection team in every school
summary_ru: 🎓 В Дубае запустили систему защиты учащихся в частных школах KHDA представила единый каркас безопасности для частных учебных заведений, включая школы, детские центры и вузы. В системе выделены три уровня риска угроз безопасности учащихся с разными процедурами реагирования. В каждой школе создадут команду защиты, в которую войдут директор и минимум два ответственных сотрудника. Они будут следить за случаями, координировать действия и взаимодействовать с властями. Каркас основан на законе о правах ребёнка и поддерживает стратегию образования Дубая до 2033 года.
